Subject: Packaging choices, gating, and rollback plan

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call last week. Per our discussion, I put together two concise packaging paths for the pilot and a recommended gating / rollback approach so you can pick the path that best fits your risk appetite. The attached Proposal_Wellspan_v3.pdf and MAP_Wellspan_v2.xlsx are the detailed versions; summary below.

Option A — Throughput-first (Dedicated)
- 12-month dedicated capacity pool (predictable throughput)
- Includes: prefix KV caching, auto-batching, per-route tracing, A/B rollout hooks
- Pros: lowest per-token unit cost at scale, consistent latency
- Cons: commit required to reach discount thresholds

Option B — Hosted + Feature Bundle
- Hosted API with feature bundle (A/B rollouts, structured output enforcement, tracing)
- Pros: no infra commit, fast ramp, simple procurement
- Cons: higher unit cost at sustained high throughput

Gating & rollback (recommended canonical plan)
- 30-day canary window for the first tranche of traffic (10–20% of calls)
- Success thresholds: <200ms p50 route latency, error rate <0.5%, cost delta <= +12% versus baseline
- Automatic fallback: if any threshold fails for 48 continuous hours, route is automatically routed to the hosted-safe variant while we remediate
- Contract term: allow one-time mid-term re-eval at month 6 with mutually agreed smoothing for usage spikes

Ask: please confirm which option you prefer and whether procurement needs a different format. If you’re leaning Dedicated, Alex, you mentioned a 12-month commitment — I flagged that in the proposal with a discount band we can finalize. If helpful I can share the limited-time onboarding credit we can attach to the pilot.

Next steps
- You: pick Option A or B (or request a hybrid).
- We: send updated SOW and highlighted MAP row for procurement.
- Proposed decision window: by Tue, Apr 19 so we can lock resources for a May kickoff.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min call to walk through the tradeoffs.

—
